summary: This program stores the number of feet each of three animals has, adds them together, and prints each count along with the total.

lines.text: A variable gives the number a name, so the rest of the program can talk about "penguin feet" instead of a bare 2.
The addition happens once and the answer is stored, so the total can be reused without recalculating it.
The f before the quotes marks an f-string, where anything inside curly braces is replaced by the value of that variable.
Showing the individual counts first and the total last makes the arithmetic easy for a reader to check.
